title: Fatima, simply
hookLine: three children, a call to prayer, and the crowd's report of the sun in 1917

cards: Type the word Fatima into a search bar. Secrets. Prophecies.
Countdown videos. Arguments about what was hidden and who hid it.
Underneath all that noise is a much quieter story: shepherd children in the hills of Portugal, a lady who asked them to pray, and a crowd in a muddy field that later told what they saw in the sky.
Today's title has a second word, and it's the important one: simply. The secrets get set down, and the question is what the children were actually asked to do.

teach.b: You've met these children before on this path. First, the children.

Lucia and her younger cousins, Francisco and Jacinta, were watching sheep near the village of Fatima when, by their account, a lady brighter than the sun appeared to them, and came back over the following months.
What she asked wasn't complicated: pray the rosary every day, pray for sinners, turn back to God. The children took it seriously in a child's way.
Francisco would slip off to pray alone; Jacinta offered small sacrifices for others. Both are now honored as saints. Second, the sun.

teach.h: THE SUN, AS THE CROWD TOLD IT.
teach.b: At the last visit, a large crowd came, in the rain. People later said the sun seemed to spin and dance and plunge toward them, and that their soaked clothes were suddenly dry.

Accounts differ, and some people present reported nothing unusual. The Church approved the apparitions, and, as you heard three days ago, no Catholic is required to believe them. Third, the message is old.

Without the drama, Fatima says what Jesus said when he first began to preach, in the Douay-Rheims of Mark's Gospel: "The time is accomplished, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent, and believe the gospel."
Repent is a call to turn around: not a new teaching, but the one Jesus opened with, repeated by children in a field. Fourth, the rosary. The daily request wasn't a crusade or a secret code.
It was beads in a pocket, prayer the size of a few minutes.
That's Fatima, simply: pray, and turn around, and start again tomorrow.

how: Catholics who honor Our Lady of Fatima pray the rosary, often daily, as the children reported she asked; pilgrims visit the shrine at Fatima in Portugal, and her feast is kept in May.

games.q: you're one of the shepherd children. the lady asks you for one thing to do every day. what is it?
o: tell no one what you saw.
games.why: by the children's account, she asked them to pray the rosary every day. Fatima, simply, is daily prayer and turning back to God.

practice: A decade of the rosary is one Our Father, ten Hail Marys and a Glory Be.

If you pray, say one now, slowly, on your fingers if you have no beads; if you don't, count ten slow breaths on your fingers, and with each, name one thing you'd like to turn away from, or turn toward.

wordCard.voice: Fatima. The Portuguese village where shepherd children said a lady asked for daily prayer and conversion, and where a crowd reported a sign in the sun. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: pray and repent. An old message, carried by children in a field. Until tomorrow.
